p10_b0.ocr: In the context of evaluating the diverse training backgrounds that contribute to the understanding of immune system modulation, the data presented in the table serves as a critical resource. The responses to the question "What training do you have?" highlight the varying degrees of formal education, work experience, and life experience among participants. Notably, the metrics of "First response" and "Receptor" provide insight into how different educational and experiential backgrounds influence knowledge of specific biochemical pathways and their associated functions.

p10_b1.ocr: For example, respondents with formal education in immunology may demonstrate a more comprehensive understanding of the role of receptors like PAR-1 and signaling pathways involving CCL2, PKC/c-SRC/EGFR/MEK/ERK/AP-1. This knowledge is crucial for elucidating the activation mechanisms of monocytes, memory T cells, and dendritic cells within various therapeutic contexts. Understanding these relationships not only enhances academic discourse but also informs treatment strategies aimed at optimizing immune responses. The findings underscore the importance of diverse training in advancing both research and clinical applications in immunotherapy.
